rows.grounds: compound of vyādha (hunter), vyāja (guise), anucita (fitting), kṛt (acting), and tāvaka (yours); final o' marks sandhi with following akhila
compound of akhila (all, initial a elided in sandhi), tuṣṭi (satisfaction), and kṛt (causing)

items.question: How does adopting the fitting guise of a hunter bring satisfaction to all?
premises: The lord assumes the fitting guise of a hunter.
This manifestation is identified as belonging to the lord.
The action results in satisfaction for all beings.
items.inference: Therefore the lord's assumption of a humble guise serves to bring universal satisfaction.
uncertainties: The specific mythic episode alluded to by the hunter guise is not explicit in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: Acting as yours in the fitting guise of a hunter, he brings satisfaction to all.
